subject: Science
title: Day and night
subtopics: What we see in the day
objectives: Children will say what happens in the day and what happens at night.
Children will match pictures to day or night.
content: What we see in the day, what we see at night, and why we sleep and rest.
teachingActivities: Use large day and night pictures; link to children’s own routines; sing a goodnight song; be sensitive to different family routines; never frighten children about the dark.
learnerActivities: Sort pictures into day and night and say that we sleep at night.
resources: Day and night pictures: sun, moon, stars, birds, a bed, a school
A yellow and a dark blue sheet
A soft toy and a blanket
assessment: Observe whether each child sorts pictures into day and night and says we sleep at night.
expectedOutcomes: Sorts pictures into day and night.
Says that we sleep at night.

lessons.title: What we see in the day
lessons.subject: Science
lessons.subtopic: What we see in the day
objectives: Children will name things we see in the day.
successCriteria: Names the sun and one other daytime thing
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can say light and dark and have made shadows.
resources: Pictures of the sun, a bird, a school and children playing
lessons.starter: Lay a yellow sheet and say "This is the day. The sun shines. We play and learn."
teacherActivities: Show each picture and say what we do or see in the day.
Say "In the day we see the sun and the birds."
Act out waking up, going to school and playing.
Ask "What do we see in the day?"
learnerActivities: Children look and say the names.
Children point to the sun and the bird.
Children act out each part of the day.
Child points or says a word.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each picture and say what we do or see in the day. Children: Children look and say the names.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "In the day we see the sun and the birds." Children: Children point to the sun and the bird.
Step 3. Teacher: Act out waking up, going to school and playing. Children: Children act out each part of the day.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "What do we see in the day?" Children: Child points or says a word.

practical.title: Day pictures
steps: Lay pictures on a yellow sheet.
Say what we see and do in the day.
practical.safety: Keep the floor clear for acting and never look at the sun. Supervise movement.

differentiation.support: Point to the picture and say the word together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to name three things they do in the day.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do in the day?

lessons.conclusion: Wave to the sun and say "Hello, day."
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about what you do during the day with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name things we see in the day" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Good morning, sun. It is time for the day.

lessons.title: What we see at night
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will name things we see at night.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can say light and dark and have made shadows.
resources: Pictures of the moon, stars, a bed and a sleeping child
lessons.starter: Lay a dark blue sheet and say "This is the night. We see the moon and stars."
teacherActivities: Show each picture and say what we see at night.
Put paper stars on the dark sheet and count them.
Say "At night it is dark and quiet."
Ask "What do we see at night?"
learnerActivities: Children look and say the names.
Children place stars and count.
Children say shh and whisper.
Child points or says a word.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each picture and say what we see at night. Children: Children look and say the names.
Step 2. Teacher: Put paper stars on the dark sheet and count them. Children: Children place stars and count.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "At night it is dark and quiet." Children: Children say shh and whisper.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "What do we see at night?" Children: Child points or says a word.

practical.title: Night sky
steps: Put stars and a moon on it.
practical.safety: Do not make the room too dark and never frighten children about the night. Stay close to every child.

differentiation.support: Place the stars together and say the word.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say what the moon looks like.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we see at night?
Is it light or dark at night?

lessons.homeConnection: Look at the moon and stars together at night.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name things we see at night" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Day or night?
lessons.subject: Science
lessons.subtopic: What we see in the day
objectives: Children will sort pictures into day and night.
successCriteria: Puts a picture on the correct sheet
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can say light and dark and have made shadows.
resources: A yellow sheet and a dark blue sheet
lessons.starter: Show the two sheets and say "One is for day. One is for night."
teacherActivities: Pick up a picture of the sun and put it on the day sheet.
Pick up a picture of the moon and put it on the night sheet.
Let each child pick a picture and choose a sheet.
learnerActivities: Children watch and say day.
Children watch and say night.
Child sorts the picture.
Children say day or night.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Pick up a picture of the sun and put it on the day sheet. Children: Children watch and say day.
Step 2. Teacher: Pick up a picture of the moon and put it on the night sheet. Children: Children watch and say night.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child pick a picture and choose a sheet. Children: Child sorts the picture.
Step 4. Teacher: Check each sheet together. Children: Children say day or night.

practical.title: Day and night sort
steps: Put two sheets on the floor.
Put it on the day or night sheet.
practical.safety: Use large pictures and keep the floor clear. Supervise turns.

differentiation.support: Offer two pictures and say the time first.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to add one more picture to each sheet.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Does the sun come out in the day?
Do stars come out at night?

expectedOutcomes: Sorts pictures into day and night
lessons.conclusion: Put the sheets away and say "Day and night."
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about day and night activities at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "sort pictures into day and night" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Sleep and rest
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will say that we sleep at night and that sleep helps us grow.
successCriteria: Acts out getting ready for bed
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can say light and dark and have made shadows.
resources: A soft toy and a blanket
Pictures of washing, pyjamas, a story and sleeping
lessons.starter: Hold a soft toy and say "Teddy is tired. It is night. It is time to sleep."
teacherActivities: Show pictures of the bedtime steps and say them in order.
Act out washing, putting on pyjamas and a story.
Put Teddy to bed and say "Sleep helps us grow."
learnerActivities: Children look and say the steps.
Children act each step.
Children whisper and tuck Teddy in.
Children lie down quietly.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show pictures of the bedtime steps and say them in order. Children: Children look and say the steps.
Step 2. Teacher: Act out washing, putting on pyjamas and a story. Children: Children act each step.
Step 3. Teacher: Put Teddy to bed and say "Sleep helps us grow." Children: Children whisper and tuck Teddy in.
Step 4. Teacher: Rest quietly for one minute. Children: Children lie down quietly.

practical.title: Bedtime for Teddy
steps: Make a bed for Teddy with a blanket.
practical.safety: Keep the area calm and ensure each child can see an adult at all times. Do not make children lie down if they are anxious.

differentiation.support: Act out the steps together beside the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell their own bedtime steps.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Says that we sleep at night
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about your child’s bedtime routine and say goodnight.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say that we sleep at night and that sleep helps us grow" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 4 day and night check
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child sorts day and night and talks about sleep.
successCriteria: Sorts pictures into day and night
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can say light and dark and have made shadows.
lessons.starter: Sing the day and night song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: day, night and sleep.
At each station ask "Is it day or night?" and "What do we do?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child answers with a word or action.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: day, night and sleep. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "Is it day or night?" and "What do we do?" Children: Child answers with a word or action.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Day and night stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Use soft toys and large pictures.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use two pictures.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to tell a friend about day and night.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: sorts pictures into day and night; names things seen at night; says we sleep at night.

questions.question: Is the sun out at night?
What do we do at night?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 4
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about day and night at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child sorts day and night and talks about sleep" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
